enablers.description: Optional. Populated by the dedicated enabler pass, which runs after the reconciler and augments this artefact rather than overwriting it. A pre-pass landscape simply omits this field.

unconfirmed_foundations.description: Optional. Checklist foundations the corpus never mentioned either way, so they are explicit gaps to confirm with the client rather than fabricated enablers.

enabler_basis.description: Provenance for the enabler pass ONLY. Present when the enabler pass ran over cleansed sources beyond the signed revision's own source list, which is allowed because that pass is detection-only: it never adds, removes or alters an opportunity. Its presence means the enablers and unconfirmed_foundations in this artefact rest on a WIDER evidence base than the opportunities do, and anything reading this artefact must say so rather than implying one corpus behind both. Absent means both rest on the same sources.

revision_source_count.description: How many sources the signed revision carries. The opportunities rest on these.

additional_sources.description: Confirmed sources outside the signed revision that the enabler pass also read. Every one has a manifest entry, so none bypassed the confirmation gate.

opportunity.description: An evidenced opportunity always publishes, whether or not the evidence supported an impact/effort judgement. It carries EITHER a full `prioritisation` OR an `ungradeable_reason`, never neither and never both: failing to grade something is not a reason to drop the finding.

ungradeable_reason.description: Set instead of `prioritisation` when the evidence genuinely does not support an impact/effort judgement. States WHY, in the grader's own words. This is an honest outcome, not a failure: the opportunity is still evidenced (verified source_refs and a statement) and still publishes in opportunities[]; only the secondary impact/effort judgement is withheld rather than fabricated.

likely_levers.description: The distinct kinds of fix this opportunity's own sources pointed to. A SET, not a single value: when two sources describe the same work and one points at automation while another points at a model, both readings are evidence and collapsing them to a winner would discard the disagreement. Absent means no source said anything about the remedy, which is the common and honest case. Runner-derived from the member observations' likely_lever, never a model judgement at this level, and ADVISORY: the real decision belongs to the consultant against a confirmed bottleneck. Exists so the portfolio can show a fix that needs no model BEFORE anyone pays to deep-map it.

work_statuses.description: The distinct work-status signals carried by this opportunity's member observations. The runner preserves disagreement rather than choosing one status: in_flight and stalled mean work is underway, while already_solved means the source says it is done.

evidenced_prioritisation.description: The impact and effort grade supported by the evidence before a signed consultant override changed the published prioritisation.

prioritisation_override.description: The signed consultant decision that changed the published prioritisation. It records either the evidenced impact and effort bands or that the opportunity was ungradeable before the override.

scale.description: Quantified scale (cadence, load, headcount) carried by this opportunity's own sources, one entry per source that gave any. A list rather than one merged value: two people describing the same work often quantify it differently, and that disagreement is evidence about the work rather than noise.

held_by.description: Who actually does this work, per source that said so. Key-person concentration is an urgency and capacity signal.

prioritisation.description: Where this opportunity sits on impact vs effort, so the room can triage the portfolio. Both are model JUDGEMENTS with the basis stated; neither is a measured number. Impact weighs how much addressing it is worth from the evidence (cadence, breadth of people or functions touched, evidenced pain, strategic weight). Effort weighs how hard it is to stand up (a policy or habit change is low, a configuration is medium, a bespoke build or integration or a blocked dependency is high). Ground both in what the sources actually show; never invent a basis that is not evidenced.

impact_rationale.description: The basis for the level, not a restatement of it. Generously bounded rather than tight: a cap that rejects a considered answer loses the whole grade, and an opportunity with no grade drops out of the impact-versus-effort triage entirely. 1500 characters is roughly 250 words, far more than a good rationale needs, and exists only to stop a runaway response.

effort_rationale.description: The basis for the level, not a restatement of it. Generously bounded rather than tight: a cap that rejects a considered answer loses the whole grade, and an opportunity with no grade drops out of the impact-versus-effort triage entirely. 1500 characters is roughly 250 words, far more than a good rationale needs, and exists only to stop a runaway response.

grade_pair.description: The impact and effort bands preserved inside a prioritisation override when a prior evidence-backed grade existed.

enabler.description: A cross-cutting foundation (data, access, identity, security, adoption, integration or governance) that gates one or more opportunities. Deliberately carries NO impact/effort/prioritisation and no bottleneck: an enabler's importance is not a model judgement, it is DERIVED by the runner at render time from the impact grades of the opportunities it unlocks. The model asserts only its readiness state and the opportunity ids it evidences unlocking.

readiness.description: The evidenced state of the foundation itself, never a score: in_place (solidly there), partial (exists but incomplete), blocked (exists but not usable, e.g. behind an access barrier), gap (does not exist).

unlocks.description: Opportunity ids this foundation gates, in whole or in part. The runner's derived-importance render ("unblocks N opportunities, M high-impact") is computed from this list, never stored here.

unconfirmed_foundation.description: A curated checklist foundation the corpus said nothing about, one way or the other. Deliberately carries NO source_refs: it makes no evidenced claim, it records a gap in what was said, so it must never be confused with an enabler.
